notes: THE F1 TRAP. 367.96 is printed in the largest box on the page; the payable is 69.62. derive_amount_payable and resolve_carried_balance are wired on total_printed (Task 11); prior_balance_basis comes from the pack's billing-convention table via apply_billing_conventions, registered at afterExtraction. bill_to_name (Task 8) reads the remittance stub's LEFT column off the row it shares with the payee name: EDCO prints customer and payee side by side on one set of rows, so 'EDCO WASTE & RECYCLING SERVICE' at anchor_occurrence 'mid_line' (the only one of its three occurrences that does not begin its line - the letterhead at top=33.3 and '... FOR SERVICE AT:' at top=304.0 are both line-heads) sits on the customer name's own row, and same-row + text returns the customer's cell once _apply_field drops the anchor's words. Anchoring on the VENDOR's name to read the CUSTOMER's is not GUARDRAIL 9's anchor-is-value, and it is the same anchor/occurrence remit_address already uses. No label exists anywhere near the name and every top region returns EDCO's own letterhead first, which is why this persona shipped without the selector. Moving the field off resolve_bill_to_alias's roster rung is the point: measured over all 28 real EDCO samples the selector reads the customer's own rendering rather than the roster's, so bill_to_mismatch can now fire where the roster rung could only ever agree with itself. It fires correctly on EDCO's own misprints of the client name - NORTHSTRAY RECYCLING (823282AUG25, 823282SEP25) and NORTHSTART RECYCLING (176024OCT25) - and correctly does NOT fire on NORTHSTAR RECYCLING CO (968397OCT25), which bill_to_matches_roster accepts. KNOWN DEFECT, 1 of 28, found by the whole-branch review and NOT fixed as of this commit. An earlier draft of this note cited 709223OCT25's SYSCO FOODS-SAN DIEGO reading as evidence the selector works. It is the opposite. That document is billed to NORTHSTAR RECY and its bill_to_address on the very same record correctly reads the Northstar block, so the record contradicts itself about who it is billed to, and the bill_to_mismatch it raises is FALSE. The cause is a per-document data-entry variation, not a layout the selector mis-locates: EDCO's customer block is normally NAME / SERVICE-AT DESCRIPTOR / STREET / CITY (top=164.93/176.93/188.93/200.93), and on this one document the first two lines are SWAPPED - the descriptor SYSCO FOODS-SAN DIEGO sits on the anchor's row and the party NORTHSTAR RECY one row below. Both orderings print four lines, so the party is not at a fixed index, and the anchor row itself is correct on all 28. Constraining the pattern to a party-name SHAPE (the idiom windstream.json uses) does NOT fix it and was measured, not assumed: run against all 28 samples plus the gold document, the anchored shape ^([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9&.,'()/#-]{1,29} [A-Za-z0-9 &.,'()/#-]{1,44})$ returns exactly what pattern 'text' returns on every one of them, SYSCO FOODS-SAN DIEGO included - it is a well-formed two-token party name in the correct position. Nothing in the closed region/pattern vocabulary separates it from the real party; only a semantic check (the roster) can, which is the rung this selector deliberately moves off. Fixing it is a selector-design decision, deferred to the human partner rather than guessed at.
